tools.description: Read the next part of a cached webpage without another upstream request.
tools.name: web-fetch-mcp_fetch_continue

tools.description: Fetch a page and return its links (text + href) for navigation.
tools.name: web-fetch-mcp_fetch_links

tools.description:
Fetch a page and return its content (alias of web_fetch).

Accepts the same arguments as web_fetch: `url`, `format` (markdown/text/html),
`max_chars`.  Provided because some MCP hosts call the tool fetch_page.
tools.name: web-fetch-mcp_fetch_page

tools.description:
Capture a webpage screenshot, automatically paging oversized pages.

One MCP call returns either one full-page PNG or multiple numbered PNG
sections with signed download/resource links. Firefox scrolls down the
page and divides oversized pages vertically (and horizontally if needed)
instead of making one huge image. Each section reports its page position;
adjacent sections overlap, and vertical cuts favor gaps between text lines.
The response explicitly says whether coverage is complete or partial and
reports page dimensions and any stopping limit. Infinite-scroll sites may
be partial. Uses the same public-URL checks as web_fetch. This is a visual
capture, not extracted text or print-to-PDF.
tools.name: web-fetch-mcp_web_capture

tools.description:
Fetch a page as Markdown/text/HTML, or return an intact file download.

Local-first fallback: direct HTTP, Obscura, Firefox, then Bright Data.
Paper landing pages prominently identify advertised full-text, errata,
and supplemental links. Attachments are not automatically fetched.

`format`: "markdown" (default), "text", or "html".
`max_chars`: cap on the returned content; 0 uses the server default.
Long pages include a continuation token. `extractor`: auto, trafilatura,
or conservative. `refresh` bypasses the short-lived result cache.
tools.name: web-fetch-mcp_web_fetch

tools.description: Report which fetch engines are available and the server config.
tools.name: web-fetch-mcp_web_fetch_health
